title: A Garden for the Choir
premise: Ansel Joubert has spent twelve years as the king's food-taster, dosing himself with poisons until his body is a ledger of survivals, safe inside a valley where magic cannot cross. When prayers to the old gods begin to be answered, Ansel learns the truth: the king died years ago, and the thing wearing his crown has been feeding on the kingdom's memories, erasing anyone who noticed. Ansel's immunity—built from swallowed deaths—makes them the only person whose memories the creature cannot digest, and the only one who can carry the unbinding rite past its wards. Guided by Sera, a disgraced priestess who once served the old gods and loved Ansel before duty parted them, they must reach the crown itself before the harvest of memories completes at midwinter. In the end, Ansel gives up their own accumulated immunity—the record of every poison survived—to fuel the unbinding, freeing the kingdom but leaving them mortal, forgetful, and finally free to leave the valley with Sera.
about_author: Wendell Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing medieval herbals and poison gardens before turning to fiction. They write in a converted greenhouse, surrounded by plants that are mostly legal.

chapters.title: The Taster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet Ansel at the royal table, tasting dishes laced with slow poisons, reciting internally the list of toxins their body has learned to survive. A new servant delivers wine that tastes of nothing—and Ansel's memory of that morning goes blank for an hour. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine; the first crack in a life built on control.

chapters.title: Prayers with Answers
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. In the capital's forgotten shrine, Sera lights a candle to an old god out of habit—and receives an answer for the first time in twenty years. The god speaks in her dead mother's voice, warning that the harvest has begun. Emotional beat: terror and longing entwined; faith returning like an old wound reopening.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Summoned to taste privately for the king, Ansel notices the monarch never blinks and remembers nothing older than three years. A dropped goblet reveals no reflection where the king's should be. Ansel flees, realizing why servants vanish. Emotional beat: vertigo—the protector role inverted; the taster realizes he must protect everyone from the king.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forbids
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera finds Ansel hiding in the magic-dead valley where he was born, the only place the crown-thing cannot follow. She explains the bargain struck generations ago: the valley's emptiness bought the kingdom's blindness. Old love resurfaces between accusations. Emotional beat: bitter tenderness; two people measuring how much they've paid to survive.

chapters.title: Immunity as Inheritance
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The old god contacts Ansel through a dream of his grandmother's kitchen, revealing that every poison survived left a mark the creature cannot digest—Ansel's memory is armored. But using it means walking out of the valley, surrendering safety forever. Emotional beat: reluctant acceptance; courage chosen rather than felt.

chapters.title: Road of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Ansel and Sera travel toward the capital through villages already half-harvested, where people smile too widely and cannot name their children. They gather surviving believers as allies. An ambush by hollowed guards forces their first fight together. Emotional beat: mounting urgency; love rekindling in the space between dangers.

chapters.title: The Price of the Priestess
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Captured and brought before the crown-thing, Sera is offered her heart's desire—her mother's voice, her lost faith made whole—in exchange for betraying Ansel. She pretends to accept, learning the ritual's final requirement: a willing sacrifice of protected memory. Emotional beat: temptation and resolve; duty and love pulling opposite directions.

chapters.title: Midwinter Table
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. On the longest night, the creature begins the final harvest feast, the whole court seated as guests and food alike. Ansel infiltrates as taster, poisoning nothing, carrying instead the rite hidden in a recipe only he remembers. Sera breaks free as the first course is served. Emotional beat: cold clarity under pressure; the servant outwaiting the throne.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the crown itself, Ansel offers his immunity—every survived death, every armored memory—as fuel while Sera sings the unbinding. The creature fights back with Ansel's own worst recollections. He lets them go, one by one, choosing emptiness over captivity. The king's true corpse crumbles; the crown falls silent. Emotional beat: sacrificial climax; grief and release inseparable.

chapters.title: A Garden for the Choir
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, epilogue-like. Spring. Ansel remembers little of what he sacrificed but keeps a written ledger anyway, habit outliving need. He and Sera plant a garden over the ruined shrine where the freed small gods now sing quietly. He leaves the valley—not because he must, but because he can. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; survival transformed into living.
